articles.title: Rob Lowe Says ‘St. Elmo’s Fire’ Sequel Is Still ‘In the Works,’ Confirms There’s a Script: ‘All of Us Actors Want to Do It’
articles.summary: Rob Lowe finally has an update on the long-discussed “St. Elmo’s Fire” sequel. “It is definitely in the works, for sure,” the actor said when asked about the project’s current status during a “Watch What Happens Live” appearance on Sunday.
body: While Lowe didn’t give much away, the news that the sequel is making progress is the latest update fans of the 1985 classic have been waiting on since the film was first announced in 2024. The “Parks and Recreation” actor told Entertainment Tonight that he’d “met with the studio” and had “been talking about doing it for about four months.” “But it’s very, very, very, very, very early stages,” he added. “So we will see.” Related Stories. 'Disclosure Day' Sets Peacock Streaming Release Date. 'Gremlins 3' Delayed to 2028 by Warner Bros.

Variety previously reported that NBC was developing a series adaptation of the film back in 2019, though it never materialized. Josh Berman had been attached to write and executive produce, along with Chris King. At the time, the series was described as a modern adaptation of the film that showcases a group of close friends struggling with career, commitment and the responsibilities of adulthood.
Released in 1985, “St. Elmo’s Fire” starred Lowe, Moore, Emilio Estevez, Andrew McCarthy, Ally Sheedy, Judd Nelson and others. Joel Schumacher directed and co-wrote the script with Carl Kurlander.

articles.title: Century-old silent film made in New Hampshire found in Japan antique shop
articles.summary: Billy B Van’s 1919 comedy Van-ar-chy found by student in Sendai will be shown in early November in New Hampshire. A silent comedy filmed in New Hampshire more than a century ago was recently found in Japan, and plans have been set to show the film in early November in the state where it was…
body: Van-ar-chy, a 1919 film starring the US entertainer and film-maker Billy B Van, was rediscovered by Kohei Okita, a film student in Sendai, Japan. While researching early cinema related to the word “anarchy”, Okita bought several old film reels at an antique store in Japan and found the comedy starring Van, whom he did not recognize, according to a Van-ar-chy news release.

Internet searching then connected Okita with John Tariot, a Van archivist. Tariot identified the comedy as Van-ar-chy, one of Van’s films made in New Hampshire in the communities of Newport and Sunapee.

Van, who lived from 1870 to 1950, began his career performing on Broadway and in vaudeville before turning to film-making. He later founded the Equity Motion Picture Company and opened a studio in Georges Mills, New Hampshire, where he produced silent comedies filmed around the Lake Sunapee area.

articles.title: Former ‘South Park’ Writer Launches Site to Expose Information About Cornell University Sexual Assault Case: ‘There Will Be Accountability’
articles.summary: Following the news that a former Cornell student had accused seven men of raping and drugging her at a frat house party in October 2024 — and none faced legal consequences — former “South Park” writer Toby Morton has launched a website dedicated to documenting the account of the woman (identified…
body: While much of the site remains under construction, Morton shared a separate statement to Instagram about his work, explaining that while he is “not a journalist,” that fact makes him “more dangerous.” “I have no limits, no boundaries, nobody to tell me I’ve gone too far,” he wrote.

Information around the event has begun to surface following a lawsuit filed by the student against the college two weeks ago, which claimed that the school failed to protect her and prevent the alleged assault. At the time, following an investigation by the university, two of the men were expelled, while the other five received lesser punishment. The lawsuit claims that some of them were able to write essays to the school to reduce their disciplinary action, according to her attorney.

On Sunday, Florence Pugh posted a statement on social media in response to the case, describing the incident as a “horrific act.” “I’m feeling uneasy and sick and anxious,” she wrote. “I’m processing quietly and watching everything and everyone and every man.”
In addition to writing credits on “South Park,” Morton voiced Scott Tenorman on the show. He also wrote on “Mad TV.”

articles.title: John Le Carré’s Cold War Spymaster George Smiley Returns in First Look at Matthew Macfadyen in ‘Legacy of Spies’
articles.summary: John Le Carré’s legendary British Cold War spy George Smiley, last seen on screens in the acclaimed film “Tinker Tailer Soldier Spy’ (played by Gary Oldman, coincidentally now starring as another fictitious agent in “Slow Horses”), has finally returned.
body: In “Legacy of Spies,” when Leamas recruits Doris Quinz (Islamoğlu), a young and dynamic East German woman, to smuggle high-value Stasi documents into the West, it sets in motion a series of events that threaten to explode in the crucible of Cold War Berlin. Pursuing Leamas and Doris are Josef Fiedler (Brühl) and Hans-Dieter Mundt (Kammerer), two Stasi operatives whose ferocious desire to shut down the intelligence leak is matched only by their internal rivalry and an iron will to outmatch each other.

Pulled into the action is Liz Gold (O’Casey), an idealistic young woman whose courage and conviction force Leamas to navigate a world where loyalties fracture and betrayal is inevitable. Behind the scenes, the brilliant and taciturn spymaster Smiley orchestrates operations while the elusive Soviet mastermind Karla looms in the shadows, setting the stage for a conflict that will define a generation. As per the description: “Personal lives become collateral in a ruthless intelligence war, and as the lines between duty and love begin to blur, every emotion becomes a weapon.”

articles.title: Mohammad Rasoulof, O Mipo to Receive Tokyo Film Festival’s Kurosawa Akira Award
articles.summary: Mohammad Rasoulof, the Iranian filmmaker who secretly left his country in 2024 after being sentenced to eight years in prison, will receive the Kurosawa Akira Award at the 39th Tokyo International Film Festival. He will share the honor with director O Mipo.
body: The committee praised the “humanist perspective” of his recent work, “which portrays even those who perpetrate oppression as ordinary citizens.”
“Receiving the Kurosawa Award is a great honor for me,” Rasoulof said. “His films are profound explorations of the human condition and the moral choices we make in moments of crisis.”

Ostarted out as a script supervisor after working at Obayashi Nobuhiko’s production company. She made her feature debut in 2006 with “The Sakais’ Happiness.” “The Light Shines Only There” (2014) won her best director at the Montreal World Film Festival and was Japan’s Oscar submission. “Being Good” (2015) was named best Asian film at the Moscow International Film Festival. After a nine-year gap in which she had two children, she came back with “Living in Two Worlds” (2024), which competed at Shanghai. Her latest, “How Dare You?” (2025), played in competition at Zlín.

articles.title: Pandora’s Legacy review – fascinating profile of silent film legend GW Pabst
articles.summary: Through intimate letters and family interviews, this probing documentary about the Austrian film-maker reveals a complicated figure. A titan of silent cinema, Austrian director GW Pabst left behind a treasure trove of classics.
body: Far from a hagiographic portrait, Christlieb’s film reveals Pabst to be a complicated and patriarchal figure. His grandchildren – Marion, Daniel and Ben – describe the great film-maker as a distant figure, who instilled fear rather than love in his two sons. Pabst’s films have been praised for their modern and strong-willed female characters, yet in private he forbade Gertrude from pursuing her own acting aspirations. She also reluctantly underwent numerous abortions – seven in total – so as not to derail her husband’s career.

articles.title: Crushed review – Steve Oram is priestly lead in harrowing Bangkok-set child-abduction thriller
articles.summary: A priest investigates his daughter’s kidnapping in Thailand in this Paul Schrader-esque inquiry into spiritual nihilism. ‘He’s American, a little bit overweight, sweaty, a little bit camp, creepy.” As far as descriptions of border-hopping paedophiles go, this seems a little on the nose.
body: Pastor to a mixed Anglo-Thai congregation, Father Daniel has a young daughter, Olivia (Margaux Dietrich), with wife May (Nattapohn Rawddon). At a sleepover, Olivia is traumatised when her friend’s older brother shows her a “crush” video of a kitten being stomped by a scantily clad floozy. So when her own cat Missy goes awol, she is convinced the same lady is responsible, and asks her dad how God could let it happen. The family mobilise to track down Missy, but Olivia in turn disappears one day after school, kicking off Father Daniel’s own test of faith.

There could have been a very different version of Crushed, if Liam Neeson had signed on with his special set of ecumenical skills. But Rumley holds the vengeance angle at bay, subtly foreshadowing Olivia’s ordeal with the implied horror of the squashed furballs filtering through her nightmares, and using clever juxtaposition to slyly compare and contrast her father’s lofty ideals with the surrounding scrappy reality. At one point, after refusing to play the Beatles’ profane songs, Father Daniel’s acoustic guitar version of All Creatures Great and Small soundtracks Olivia’s pet search on the streets.

articles.title: Sylvester Stallone Reacts to Biopic ‘I Play Rocky’: “I’m Not Dead Yet. Aren’t We Jumping the Gun?”
articles.summary: During a conversation at 92NY, Stallone complimented Anthony Ippolito — who plays a young version of the star in the film — saying, "I actually thought it was me the first moment."
body: Sylvester Stallone is weighing in on seeing his life’s story retold on the big screen in the upcoming biopic I Play Rocky.

The film, which premiered to much fanfare at the Toronto International Film Festival earlier this month, follows the making of 1976’s Rocky, with Anthony Ippolito playing a young version of Stallone as he develops and pushes the film through a tumultuous production.

The star emphasized he has “nothing to do” with the movie, which was directed by Peter Farrelly. “I said, ‘I’ll just sit back and watch.’ I talked to the kid. I said, ‘If you want any questions, here I am,’ and that was it. But they did it all on their own,” as Stallone joked that in seeing Ippolito’s portrayal, “I go, ‘Do I talk like that?’ Now I get it. Now I get it.”

Elsewhere in the conversation, Stallone spoke about what it’s like for him to watch the Rocky movies now (“It’s like you look at a photo of yourself, everyone else likes it, but you go [growl]”) and revealed he’s trying to get Amazon to let him recut 1990’s Rocky V, calling the movie “a thorn in my side.”

articles.title: ‘Should have garnered the actor an Oscar’: why Liar Liar is my feelgood movie
articles.summary: The latest in our series of writers paying tribute to the films they watch when they need a lift is an appreciation of Jim Carrey’s manic 90s comedy. To be completely honest, whenever anybody asks what my favorite movies are, my list has some typical standbys: Goodfellas and It’s a Wonderful Life…
body: The movie (for the lack of a better word) lies on the bedrock of a simple premise: a lawyer and doting father is physically unable to tell an untruth due to a birthday wish. In the hands of a less competent creative team and cast, Liar Liar would have been yet another forgettable piece of 90s comedy junk; destined for the bottom of a discount VHS bin, forgotten as the years trudged on. But largely thanks to an unbelievable performance courtesy of Carrey, who was working with a smart and peppy script, the film ascends into rarefied air.

The bellylaugh-o-meter breaks its springs on a regular basis throughout its brisk 86-minute runtime. In fact, it’s on par, or even surpassing, fellow comedy powerhouses such as Airplane! and The Naked Gun when it comes to the sheer volume of gags, set pieces and jokes. Tom Shadyac, the director, who previously directed Carrey in his 1993 breakout Ace Ventura: Pet Detective, wisely unleashes Carrey, who spins out and around the scenery like the Tasmanian Devil, remarkably combining such a manic and energetic performance with one grounded in pure emotion.

articles.title: ‘South Park’ Alum Behind Viral Political Websites Targets Men Named in Cornell Chi Phi Lawsuit
articles.summary: Toby Morton says photos, employer info and billboards are coming for the seven defendants, and for Cornell administrators he says "failed miserably."
body: Over the weekend, Toby Morton spent time updating his latest and perhaps most controversial website, which names and posts a threat to the seven men named in a civil rape case filed two weeks ago in New York that has grabbed the nation and led to outcry about sexual assault over the past few days.

The simple website contains a page that names the seven defendants in Jane Doe’s suit and contains blank boxes that indicate that photos of them will be uploaded —and potentially pages for the men who are facing accusations.

“The [website] will bring together her account, the lawsuit, public records, documented reporting, institutional responses and additional verified information as it becomes available,” Morton wrote on the site. “The goal is not to be first. The goal is to build a record that can withstand scrutiny. This will take time. I will be careful. It will be documented.”

Morton wrote that as new photos and information are shared, he’ll be including members of the Cornell administration who he said “failed miserably.” He also anticipated that he’d be conflated with a journalist investigating the men accused of assaulting the young woman while students at Cornell.
points: Toby Morton says photos, employer info and billboards are coming for the seven defendants, and for Cornell administrators he says "failed miserably."

articles.title: Slipknot fans hit back after Marilyn Manson announced as support act for UK show
articles.summary: The heavy metal band will be joined by the US rock musician during their London show.
body: Heavy metal band Slipknot have announced a new world tour, with Marilyn Manson due to appear as a support act.
The eight-piece group, known for performing in masks, will be joined by the US rock musician during their shows at London's Wembley Stadium and multiple dates of the South American leg of the tour.
Some fans have reacted angrily to the news and said they will not attend the shows over past sexual abuse accusations against the 57-year-old.
Manson, real name Brian Warner, has always strongly denied any allegations against him.
